observed_mechanics: 0x008414d0: MOV EAX,dword ptr [ECX + 0xf0] (8b 81 f0 00 00 00) loads the receiver word at +0xf0; it is later pushed as the second format operand.
0x008414d6: PUSH ESI saves the callee-saved register that then carries the address operand.

0x008414d7: LEA ESI,[ECX + 0xf4] (8d b1 f4 00 00 00) materialises the address of the receiver's 16-byte string header at +0xf4; this is the first (destination) argument, and it is the only way +0xf4 is reached -- no instruction dereferences [ECX + 0xf4] directly.
0x008414dd: MOV ECX,dword ptr [ECX + 0xe0] (8b 89 e0 00 00 00) loads only word 0 of the object at +0xe0 and reuses ECX as scratch; ECX is never reloaded, so the receiver is not re-entered.
0x008414e3 and 0x008414e4: PUSH EAX then PUSH ECX push exactly two variadic words, in cdecl last-push-is-first-argument order: first the +0xe0 word, then the +0xf0 word.
0x008414e5: PUSH 0x141bcb0 pushes the format-string address. ghidra_read_memory at 0x0141bcb0 returns 25 73 3a 25 64 00, i.e. the C literal "%s:%d".
0x008414ea: PUSH ESI pushes the &this+0xf4 destination, completing the four-word cdecl argument list.
0x008414eb: CALL 0x00840c20 is the only call instruction in the body; the briefing xref list agrees (one outgoing direct-call to 0x00840c20).

0x00840c20 reads arg1 with MOV ECX,[ESP+0x4], builds a va_list with LEA EAX,[ESP+0xc], calls 0x00938400 with (0x164f780, 0x400, fmt, ap), then scans 0x0164f780 for its NUL and calls 0x00454cb0 as an __thiscall member with ECX = arg1. 0x00938400 decompiles to the vsnprintf shape (size-bounded, NUL-terminating, empty format guarded by -(param_1 != 0) & param_2) and 0x00454cb0 decompiles to a bounded range assign over the words begin (word 0) and end (word 1) of the destination, with a reallocation branch through 0x00455d60.

0x00840c41..0x00840c49 leave EAX = 0x164f780 + strlen and EDX = 0x164f780 + 1, so 0x00840c4f SUB EAX,EDX yields strlen(scratch) - 1 and 0x00840c51 LEA EDX,[EAX + 0x164f780] yields the range end 0x164f780 + strlen(scratch) - 1 that is handed to 0x00454cb0. This one-byte-short range is a property of the callee 0x00840c20, not of 0x008414d0, and is modelled in the package rather than asserted as intent.
0x008414f0: MOV EAX,dword ptr [ESI] reloads the destination string's word 0 after the call, so the return value is whatever the callee left in the destination header.
0x008414f2: ADD ESP,0x10 removes the four callee argument words; 0x00840c20 ends in a plain RET, confirming caller cleanup.
0x008414f5 POP ESI / 0x008414f6 RET: unconditional straight-line return, no branch, no loop and no conditional anywhere in the 13-instruction body.
The function writes no global and touches no field of the receiver other than through the callee's destination pointer; it is otherwise pure with respect to the receiver's own words.

type_scope: package-local qualified names only; no global type record was added and no concrete ArgScript type is asserted beyond the import label
semantic_findings: Despite the import name ArgScript::FormatParser::ParseUInt, the body contains no digit test, no multiply-add accumulation, no base conversion and no integer store: it formats a "%s:%d" trace string from two receiver words and returns the destination string's begin word. The name is treated as a candidate label only, not as the recovered semantics, and the entry symbol's parse_uint spelling is a validator span binding rather than a semantic claim.
0x008414d0 is a vtable entry (the dword at 0x0141c95c) and never dispatches virtually itself: it has no indirect call, so the receiver's concrete subclass is not resolved by this function.
The two format operands are read once each and pushed once each, so the function is a single snapshot read of +0xe0 and +0xf0; there is no loop and no re-read.
ECX is clobbered by the scratch load at 0x008414dd and is never restored, which confirms the body is not re-entrant on the receiver and needs no separate callee-saved slot for it.

The return value is not the formatted text itself in the machine sense: it is the begin word of the destination string, so callers that expect a uint get a pointer re-typed as a word (the Ghidra prototype says uint).

The "%s" operand is the +0xe0 word and the "%d" operand is the +0xf0 word, so the format literal is a script-name-and-line style trace pair; that reading of the two fields' meaning is a guess and is not claimed.

runtime_gates: The native return type is unresolved between char* and uint32_t; the machine only shows a dword load classified pointer_like, and both the SDK label and the decompilation say uint.

The declared pString stack slot of the SDK prototype is never read by the body; whether real callers push an argument there is unverified, and if they do, the callee performs no stack cleanup for it (plain RET).

The strlen(scratch) - 1 range computed inside 0x00840c20 may be an intentional convention or an off-by-one in the original; nothing in the static evidence settles it and it was not exercised at runtime.
The identity and signature of the concrete 0x00840c20 in the running image were not resolved, and no virtual call site of 0x008414d0 was captured, so runtime_validation stays 0.
Ownership and lifetime of the string at this+0xf4, and whether any caller frees or reallocates it, are unresolved.

The declared types of the +0xe0 word (consumed by %s, so a char* in practice) and the +0xf0 word (consumed by %d, so a signed 32-bit int) are inferred from the format conversions, not from any write site observed in this package.

unresolved_questions: Is the native return type char* or uint32_t? Ghidra's prototype and the SDK import both say uint, yet the returned dword is the begin word of the string used as the callee's char* destination. Attempt 2 made the abi record's return_type field carry the modeled type alone ('const char*', spelled as the declaration spells it) and moved the argument to return_type_rationale, so the type field is a type again; the disagreement itself is not settled. Note that the abi category in the evidence pack is copied from this record, so agreement between it and the source is a self-consistency check, not independent corroboration -- the independent part is the machine record's own return.register_class 'pointer_like'.

FIELDS/OFFSETS: is the machine-derived receiver record wrong, or is the model wrong? The record is narrower than the body: abi_derived.receiver is shape R-DIRECT with offsets [0xe0, 0xf0] and distinct_offsets 2, while the same pack's 13-instruction listing names 0xe0, 0xf0 and 0xf4 through ECX (0xf4 via LEA ESI,[ECX + 0xf4] at 0x008414d7). The record counts only direct [ECX+disp] dereferences, so a displacement carried in a LEA is invisible to it. This package holds that the record under-reports and the model is right, and did not shrink the model to fit the bounds; the disagreement is not settled because the fix belongs in the ABI inference, which is tooling-owned.
Does any real caller push the declared pString stack argument, and if so who cleans it up given the plain RET?

What is the full extent of the FormatParser vtable beginning at 0x0141c930, and which of the 24 slots up to and including 0x5c belong to base classes? Slots 0x4c and 0x5c hold 0x00841290 (Release) and 0x008414d0 respectively, and slot 0x24 holds 0x00841490.
Is the strlen-1 range inside 0x00840c20 intentional, and what does 0x00454cb0 do with the destination when the range does not fit (the 0x00455d60 reallocation path)?
Are there writers of the words at +0xe0 and +0xf0 that would confirm their declared types (a script and a line/index respectively are guesses only)?
What is the concrete class behind the vtable at 0x0141c930 for a live FormatParser, and does the secondary table at 0x0141c97c override slot 0x5c?

GLOBALS: the body names the data address 0x0141bcb0 and nothing corroborates it -- the xref export carries no data-reference edge type and the pack's globals category is empty -- so its role as the "%s:%d" literal rests on the ghidra_read_memory byte read alone. That is sufficient for a format operand (the bytes are self-identifying) but it means no second machine witness confirms the address is a string and not a pointer to one.

Was any ABI projection ever produced for this VA? evidence.missing_sections lists ABI, so the whole observed_original_abi block was derived by hand from the disassembly and needs review against a native build.
